title: tooling(pm): ci-failure.mjs resolves a red lane's failed step to `Lane verdict` since A1; resolve the red gate names from the verdict's annotations instead
body:
Filing-gate category ①, a defect with a named landing point, made live by PR #23212 (#23191, #23177 ruling B item A1), which merged as `7aa82a3dc3`.

**Reader who acts:** the `domain:devx` execution seat.

## What is measured (by #23191's dev, on PR #23212's proof head `5301220aa`)

- Under `continue-on-error: true`, a red gate step's `conclusion` reads `success`, both in the steps context and in the jobs API `steps[].conclusion`. Only the steps-context `outcome` reads `failure`. That was job `115214618941`, step #8, "Docs anchors resolve to real headings".
- So the only failed step of a red lane is now `Lane verdict`.
- `node scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` on that head reports "failed step #68 Lane verdict". Its `substitute` block resolves that name 12 times, once per lane, to `node scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs`, which exits 3 when run locally.
- The failing gate's own command (`pnpm check:doc-anchors`) appears only in the annotation text: "gate step \"NAME\" (id ID) failed".
- The tool's docblock contract (`stepBodies`) reads: "the step name the jobs API returns resolves to the command that reproduces the failure locally". That no longer holds for a red lane.
- The log half still works: `extractLogAssertion` finds the gate's stdout above its own `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.`

## What done looks like

- When the failed step is `Lane verdict`, `ci-failure.mjs` takes the red gate names from that step's annotations and resolves each name through `stepBodies` to its own `run:` command. The `substitute` block then prints the red gates' commands, not `lane-verdict.mjs`.
- The self-test pins three things:
  - a Lane-verdict failure with N red gates resolves to N gate commands;
  - an all-success lane with a red verdict (a roster mismatch) says so, and does not resolve to nothing;
  - a pre-A1 head (a gate step with conclusion `failure`) still resolves as before.
- `references/platform-readings.md` gains the platform reading above, through the skills lane, under the governed `.claude/**` path. That part is optional here; it can ride #23201 or its own skills card.
